Document: Practice Direction – Application for a warrant under the Enterprise Act 2002
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
## Retention and copying of
        items

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Retention and copying of
        items] Items seized during the search will be retained by the
          OFT only for as long as is necessary in all the circumstances. For example,
          material seized may be retained if it will be needed –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Retention and copying of
        items] for use in evidence in a criminal trial;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Retention and copying of
        items] to satisfy the OFT’s criminal disclosure obligations; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Retention and copying of
        items] so that it may be subjected to forensic examination. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Retention and copying of
        items] Material may also be retained under the provisions of
          the Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Retention and copying of
        items] On request, the OFT will, where
          practicable, provide a copy of such material to the person from whom the
          material was seized as soon as reasonably practicable. ## Confidentiality

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Confidentiality] You should note that, subject to the safeguards in
          relation to self-incrimination and communications subject to privilege, you are not entitled to withhold a document or information by claiming
          that it is confidential. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Confidentiality] However, section 237 of the Act
          imposes limits on the disclosure of information that relates to the affairs of
          any individual or any business which has been obtained by the OFT as a result
          of using its powers of investigation under the Act, subject to certain
          exceptions. Those exceptions include the right of the OFT to disclose
          information for the purpose of facilitating the exercise by the OFT of its
          statutory function and the investigation of any criminal offence in any part of
          the UK. The relevant provisions are in Part 9 of the Act. ## Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] You are entitled to apply to the Court to vary or
          discharge the Warrant. If you intend to make such an application, you must
          first inform the named officer. An application to stop the Warrant from being
          executed must be made immediately upon it being served. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] The application must be made to the judge who issued the
          Warrant, or if he is not available, to another judge of the Chancery
          Division. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] If you are making an immediate application to stop the
          Warrant from being executed, the named officer will delay starting or
          continuing a search of the premises for a reasonable period (not exceeding two
          hours) while you make your application, provided that you –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] permit the named officer and other officers [and other accompanying persons] to enter and remain on the premises;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] keep the named officer informed of the steps you are taking in relation to the application;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] provide the named officer with contact details of the solicitor, if any, who is in receipt of your formal instructions in relation to an application to stop the Warrant being executed; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] comply with any other conditions that the named officer imposes. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] Examples of conditions that the named
          officer may impose pursuant to (4) above include –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] that you do not disturb or move any document or information that is the subject of the Warrant; and/or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application to vary or discharge
        the Warrant] you do not tell anyone other than your legal adviser about the Warrant or the investigation. ## Application under section 59
        Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application under section 59
        Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001] Your attention is drawn to section 59 of the Criminal
          Justice and Police Act 2001, which makes provision about applications relating
          to property seized in the exercise of the powers conferred by (among other
          provisions) section 194(2) of the Act. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Application under section 59
        Criminal Justice and Police Act 2001] An application under section 59 should
          be made to a judge of the Crown Court. ## Footnotes

[PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > Footnotes] 1. The named officer is the principal officer
          of the OFT who, together with other officers and accompanying persons, is
          authorised by the Warrant to exercise the powers under section 194 of the Act. His name and the names of the other officers and accompanying persons are set
          out in Schedule B to the Warrant. ## 2. See section 197 of the Enterprise Act
          2002. [PRACTICE DIRECTION –
          APPLICATION FOR A WARRANT UNDER THE ENTERPRISE ACT
          2002 > 2. See section 197 of the Enterprise Act
          2002.] Updated: Monday, 30 January 2017
